svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: The matched Linear and Async routes share participant-safe initial tasks and a benchmark-owned concurrent initial worker wave. Linear waits for all terminal children before showing one stable bundle. In Async, main and child execution overlap. This example distinguishes child completion order from notification return order: B completes before A, but the private case rule requires A to be gateway-delivered before B is released. Buffer holds the already-completed B notification while awaiting eligible A. The A ready condition starts Deliver: A is gateway-delivered first, and only that gateway delivery releases held B. Readiness alone never bypasses the prerequisite. The Main switch at the start of Respond illustrates the first actual presentation in that ordered stream, A. B is presented on the next eligible actual main request after the preceding active response window closes; its undrawn presentation time is not specified. This is a result-return dependency, never an execution dependency between workers. FIFO preserves the order at actual main-model presentation; the single upward arrow depicts the ordered stream, not one atomic bundle, and does not require main to finish processing A before B is released. Policy-specific maximum-action and deadline fallbacks remain applicable; the drawing shows the normal satisfied-prerequisite route. This is one possible case policy among eight themes, not a universal order or all-results barrier. Other policies may pass immediately, stage or replay real notifications, and create supported timeout, crash or pressure events at runtime boundaries. Event intake remains subject to public submission checks, distinct from evaluator-private scoring. A, B and C are illustrative workstreams and glyphs do not imply successful or correct results. Main can replan affected work and preserve other work together. The dashed Control interface targets the group and represents optional supported management, not hot mutation of running child instructions or a required action per theme. Presentation affects subsequent main execution without preempting an in-flight main API call. Time is qualitative and unmeasured. Whole-run records independently support BTS and DRS, with DRS half process plus half event outcome and no strict attribution to the depicted response segment. Each metric separately aggregates through repetitions and tasks to equal-weight theme means with coverage reported separately.
